observations: Photo 0 and photo 1 show the same white computerized sewing machine with an embroidery unit attached, sitting on a striped bedsheet on a black leather sofa.
The word 'brother' is printed on the front of the arm in photo 0 and photo 1.
The right side has a blue panel with a floral print, a small colour LCD and a button cluster; the LCD appears lit with an image in both photos.
A small badge above the screen in photo 1 is only faintly legible and looks like 'SE630'; it cannot be read cleanly.
Both photos carry a watermark 'ABIOLA...MACHINE' and 'Posted on Jiji', so they look like a dealer's advert photos, not shots taken for this sale.
Only the front is shown: no rear, no power cord, no foot pedal, no hoops, no accessories, no stitching sample, no receipt or warranty card.
Surfaces look clean with no visible cracks or yellowing at this resolution.

read_from: photo 1 panel badge, faint, reads like SE630

claims.claim: Brother SE630 computerized sewing and embroidery machine
claims.evidence: Brand 'brother' is legible on photo 0 and photo 1; blue floral panel and embroidery unit match the SE6xx line. The model badge in photo 1 is faint, so the exact model is only partly confirmed.
Front looks clean in photo 0 and photo 1, but photos are low resolution and show no rear, base, needle plate close up or bobbin area.
No photo can prove the casing was never opened; screw heads close up would only partly help.
The LCD looks lit, which suggests it powers on, but there is no clip of it sewing or embroidering.
No receipt or warranty card is shown in any photo.

risks.risk: Sewing or embroidery function faulty (motor, timing, embroidery arm movement, touchscreen response)
risks.proof: A clip showing the machine powered on, the touchscreen being used, and it stitching a straight seam and then running a short embroidery pattern in the hoop

risks.risk: Accessories missing: power cord, foot pedal, embroidery hoop, presser feet, bobbins
risks.proof: One flat-lay photo of every included accessory next to the machine
risks.if_unproven: as machine only with no accessories

risks.risk: Photos are watermarked dealer advert images and may not show the unit actually being sold
risks.proof: A photo of the machine with a handwritten note of today's date and the seller's name placed on it
risks.if_unproven: as unverified listing; no payment before agent inspection

risks.risk: Exact model not cleanly legible; could be a lower SE6xx variant
risks.proof: A sharp close up of the model badge and the rating plate on the back or underside with serial number
risks.if_unproven: as the lowest model in the Brother SE6xx line

risks.risk: Hidden wear or damage on the back, base, needle plate or bobbin area
risks.proof: Photos of the rear, underside and a close up of the needle plate with the bobbin cover removed
risks.if_unproven: as used with fair cosmetic wear, not like new

risks.risk: Receipt and warranty may not exist or may belong to another unit
risks.proof: Photo of the receipt and warranty card showing the serial number that matches the rating plate
risks.if_unproven: as no receipt and no warranty

proof_requests: A clip of the machine powered on, stitching a seam, then running a short embroidery pattern in the hoop
A photo with a handwritten note of today's date and the seller's name on the machine
A sharp close up of the model badge and the rear or underside rating plate with serial number
A flat-lay photo of all accessories: power cord, foot pedal, hoop, presser feet, bobbins
Photos of the rear, underside and needle plate area
Photo of the receipt and warranty card with the serial visible
response.reason: The brand Brother is legible in both photos and the machine is a computerized sewing and embroidery unit of the SE6xx type, so it can be priced at worst case as not working and without accessories. Function, accessories, receipt and the exact model stay as conditions until proven.
